title: Goal 2: Material and Source-Document Storage
body:
## Goal

Securely store original material documents, document metadata, candidate records, review history, and approved material data while maintaining traceability between source PDFs and Snowflake records.

## Problems Addressed

P1: Source Documents Are Difficult to Locate  
P2: Material Data Cannot Be Verified Against Its Source  
P3: Document and Review Status Are Not Centrally Tracked  
P4: Approved Material Data Needs Durable, Queryable Storage  

## Scope

This epic covers permanent source-document storage, operational storage in Snowflake storage, document metadata, workflow status, candidate-record storage, review history, Snowflake ingestion, audit events, duplicate prevention, retries, and source-to-record traceability.

## User stories (objectives)
- [ ] #18
- [ ] #19
- [ ] #20
- [ ] #21

## Success measure
Original PDFs and metadata can be retrieved through authorized AWS S3 access. Snowflake persists candidate records, pending workflow state, validation results and review events; only approved material data is exposed for normal analysis. Approved records retain source references and ingestion outcomes, and failed or duplicate writes preserve traceability.

title: Objective 2.1: Store original source documents and document metadata
body:
## Objective

Store original CoCs and material test reports securely with document identifiers, checksums, metadata, and retrievable storage references.

## Epic

#17

## Deliverable

A source-document storage service and operational storage in Snowflake records for original PDFs, filenames, checksums, upload information, and storage references.

## Acceptance criteria

- Store each accepted original PDF without modification.
- Store the document ID, checksum, filename, uploader, upload time, document type, and storage reference in Snowflake.
- Store source documents inside a AWS S3 Bucket.
- Record source-document storage failures.
- Prevent accidental document overwrites.
- Require authorization before protected document retrieval.
- Allow authorized users to retrieve an available source-document reference.

title: Objective 2.2: Store candidate records, workflow status, and review history
body:
## Objective

Store candidate material records, document-processing status, validation results, reviewer corrections, and review decisions in the operational storage in Snowflake.

## Epic

#17

## Deliverable

Operational storage in Snowflake tables and services for document processing, candidate records, validation results, reviewer actions, and workflow history.

## Acceptance criteria

- Store candidate material identifiers, vendor information, lot information, property values, units, and source type.
- Associate every candidate record with its source-document ID.
- Track uploaded, processing, failed, pending review, approved, and rejected statuses.
- Store validation errors and warnings.
- Store reviewer identity, decision timestamp, corrections, and approval or rejection decision.
- Enforce keys, relationships, and integrity constraints.

title: Objective 2.3: Store approved material data in Snowflake
body:
## Objective

Ingest approved material records, property values, units, and source-document references into Snowflake.

## Epic

#17

## Deliverable

Approved structured material data stored in Snowflake, with the resulting Snowflake record ID linked to the related operational candidate record and source document.

## Acceptance criteria

- Publish only approved candidate records to the approved-material dataset in Snowflake; pending/candidate records remain in Snowflake operational storage and are excluded from approved views.
- Insert approved material records into Snowflake.
- Insert related property values and units.
- Insert source-document references without storing original PDF files in Snowflake.
- Return and store the resulting Snowflake record ID.
- Prevent pending, invalid, and rejected records from being stored as approved data.

title: Objective 2.4: Maintain storage reliability and source-to-record traceability
body:
## Objective

Record storage and ingestion outcomes, prevent duplicate records, retry recoverable failures, and preserve traceability from Snowflake records to original source documents.

## Epic

#17

## Deliverable

Storage and ingestion audit records that link documents, candidate records, reviewer decisions, Snowflake record IDs, errors, retries, and duplicate-detection results.

## Acceptance criteria

- Record every Snowflake ingestion attempt, status, timestamp, and error detail.
- Link each Snowflake record to its candidate record and source document.
- Use a document checksum and record revision to prevent duplicate ingestion.
- Retry recoverable Snowflake failures within a configured retry limit.
- Record every retry attempt and final failure outcome.
- Allow authorized users to trace an approved Snowflake record back to its original source document.
